content: Micron's G11 3D NAND promises 42 Gb/mm2 and 5,400 MT/s interface speed, enabling SSDs with extreme capacity and performance.

title: Solidigm confirms plans to build a fab in the US, abandons IPO plans
content: SK hynix abandons IPO plans for Solidigm, confirms plans to build a Solidigm 3D NAND fab in the U.S.

title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia
content: Amazon has ditched its plans to build four new data centers in Loudoun County, Northern Virginia, following an outcry from local residents and officials. The land will now be repurposed for mixed and residential use.

title: China can make advanced chips without EUV, but the bill keeps growing
content: China has stretched older DUV lithography far further than expected, using multiple patterning to approach 5nm-class without EUV. But experts say the trade-offs in cost, yield, and die size mean further advancements are unlikely to be economically viable.

title: Doosan Robotics targets automakers, chipmakers as Chinese rivals cut prices
content: Doosan Robotics is focusing its sales efforts on large automotive and semiconductor manufacturers as it develops AI-powered systems capable of handling more complex factory tasks, Hyeonchang Jeon, senior manager of the company's Korea sales team, said in an interview with DIGITIMES at FIX 2026 in Daegu, South Korea.

title: Taiwan's inaugural semiconductor strike pauses as nearly 70% of Micron Taoyuan Union rejects new bonus offer
content: Taiwan's first-ever strike in the semiconductor industry has temporarily drawn to a close. A 24-hour warning strike spearheaded by Micron Technology's Taoyuan union concluded on the morning of October 23, 2026. During the action, an internal ballot saw nearly 70% of all union members sign statements opposing management's proposed compensation structure. Formal labor-management negotiations are set to resume on October 27.

title: Semco's 61-week MLCC lead times give suppliers upper hand in AI supply chain
content: Samsung Electro-Mechanics (Semco) is gaining pricing power as AI server demand extends multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) lead times beyond a year. Shortages now span consumer, automotive and industrial products, prompting customers to secure 2027 supplies.

title: Lenovo mounts AI comeback with Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 deliveries and US plant expansion
content: More than 30 years ago, Lenovo set out with a vision to bring personal computers into every household. Today, Chairman and CEO Yuanqing Yang has defined a new mission for the 42-year-old tech giant: bring artificial intelligence to every home and industry, while transforming Lenovo into an AI-native enterprise targeting over US$100 billion in annual revenue within two years.

title: Japan targets 2nm medical AI chip with IBM design, Rapidus eyed for foundry
content: Japan's Leading-edge Semiconductor Technology Center (LSTC), Hokkaido University, Fujifilm Corporation, GE HealthCare Japan, and imec announced a joint initiative in Tokyo on October 20 to develop a next-generation medical imaging system powered by a dedicated 2nm AI inference chip. The initiative aims to dramatically accelerate image processing efficiency and enable real-time computing directly on medical equipment.

title: Nvidia B300 chips reportedly surface on China Telecom-linked network, raising export-control questions
content: Israeli security firm Lava identified 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs through monitoring endpoints linked to China Telecom, a state-owned carrier. The chips are barred from sale to China under US export controls. The finding adds to questions about whether the restrictions can keep advanced AI processors out of the country, but the network data does not establish where the GPUs are physically located.

title: First chip-level device on the list: US FCC bans two devices with Huawei HiSilicon chips under new rule
content: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has banned two electronic devices from entering the US market because both contain surveillance chips made by Huawei's HiSilicon. The move marks the first time the FCC has used a new rule targeting devices whose chipmakers are deemed national security risks.

title: Samsung reportedly orders final tools for first Taylor fab as Texas site nears 2nm output cap
content: Samsung Electronics has ordered additional equipment to fill the remaining space at its first foundry fab in Taylor, Texas, a move that would lift the plant's 2nm capacity to 20,000 wafers per month in the second half of 2027, ZDNet Korea reported on October 23, citing industry sources.

title: Apple reportedly taps BOE for LCD iMac development, keeps OLED timetable in question
content: Apple has reportedly asked BOE Technology and other panel makers for technical information on LCD panels for a future iMac, raising questions about the pace of its OLED transition. The potential LCD model's launch around 2029 overlaps with industry expectations for the first OLED iMac in 2029-2030.

title: TSMC advances CoPoS packaging at Taoyuan Longtan site
content: TSMC's Longtan Science Park Phase 3 in Taoyuan is restarting after nearly three years of delays, with Taiwan's National Development Council approving its development plan on September 17, 2026. The 104.65-hectare site is expected to focus first on advanced packaging technologies such as CoPoS, joining TSMC's Chiayi AP7 and Southern Taiwan Science Park AP8 facilities as the company expands capacity to meet surging AI demand.

title: Rapidus courts US AI customers ahead of planned 2H27 2nm mass production
content: Rapidus chairman Tetsuro Higashi said the Japanese chipmaker remains broadly on track to begin mass production of 2nm chips in the second half of 2027. Winning customers remains a key challenge, and initial demand is expected to come mainly from the United States, where demand related to artificial intelligence is strong.

title: Commentary: How long can the humanoid robot bubble last? Unitree's valuation correction puts physical AI to the test
content: Concerns over a potential AI bubble are intensifying. From large language models (LLMs) and AI data centers to humanoid robots, investors are increasingly questioning when massive capital investments will translate into corresponding revenue and profits.
